patch_description:
The second program achieved superior performance (score 0.58 with test_accuracy 0.96, generalization_gap 0.04) using distinct parameters for each two-qubit gate (n_distinct_params=10). The current program reduced this to 8 by sharing xx_nn and yy_shared, but performance degraded (test_accuracy 0.89, generalization_gap 0.11).

Empirical results demonstrate that parameter economy should not override generalization quality. The recommendation to further reduce parameters contradicts observed results. I propose restoring the distinct two-qubit parameters (xx_01, xx_67, yy_23, yy_14) to recover the superior generalization characteristics of the second program while keeping the current program's beneficial structure (extra RY layer and even/odd sharing in single-qubit gates).

This balances parameter efficiency (still 10 distinct, not 12) with superior generalization and worst-group margin performance.
